title: NASA Lessons Learned Information System: correction-memory rail with infusion caveat
summary: NASA LLIS is encoded as a correction-memory rail: an official, reviewed, public lessons-learned database that stores summaries and recommendations from programs/projects. The record is deliberately paired with an audit caution: recording lessons is not the same as retrieving, applying, or engineering them into practice.

status_history.note: Promoted after rev0016 because NASA LLIS was named as open source-infrastructure debt.

subjects.name: NASA Office of the Chief Engineer / NASA Engineering Network / NASA APPEL Knowledge Services

claims.claim: NASA describes the Lessons Learned system as a database of official, reviewed lessons from NASA programs and projects, managed by the NASA Lessons Learned Steering Committee and publicly searchable through NASA Office of the Chief Engineer / NASA Engineering Network access.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction or narrows its scope.

claims.claim: NASA APPEL separates the lessons-learned lifecycle into collect, record, disseminate, and apply; it explicitly treats application/infusion into practice as a crucial step rather than assuming publication equals correction.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction or narrows its scope.

claims.claim: As encoded in this cube, LLIS is a correction-memory infrastructure record, not an effectiveness verdict: it establishes a public reviewed repository surface and leaves uptake, retrieval quality, and downstream application for audit records.
what_would_change_status: A current, source-backed evaluation of LLIS effectiveness supports stronger or weaker claims about uptake and application.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass official program pages and public dataset metadata; paired with GAO audit in MKH-MET-0007
limitations: No claim that current LLIS implementation solves lesson transfer or prevents repeated failure.

type_payload.jurisdiction_or_scope: NASA agency programs and projects; public access surface
signal_capture_model: approved lessons indexed for simple/complex search
lessons include summary of original driving event and recommendations
lifecycle includes collect, record, disseminate, and apply
reporter_protection_design: not a confidential reporting scheme; a public reviewed lessons/recommendations repository
outputs: recommendations feeding training, best practices, policies, procedures
limitations: repository existence does not prove awareness, retrieval, or application
lessons may require process engineering to become actual controls
current uptake/effectiveness not evaluated in this record
type_payload.query_value: Gives the cube a model for “lessons learned” as infrastructure, while preserving the harder question of lesson infusion and follow-through.

handling_notes: Do not treat lessons-learned infrastructure as blame infrastructure.
Respect that old audits may not represent current performance; separate historical audit from current source-infrastructure existence.

unknowns: Current LLIS usage, search quality, update cadence, and application outcomes are not audited.
Need to compare public LLIS with internal/local center repositories and formal policy/update mechanisms.
next_actions: Sample a small set of LLIS records and trace whether recommendations entered policy/procedure.
Add CSB animations as another correction-memory/public pedagogy infrastructure.
Add a current audit if available before making claims about present-day effectiveness.
